newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: EU ministers agree consumer complaints system.
newsitem.headline: EU ministers agree consumer complaints system.

text.p: Aggrieved consumers will be able to seek redress throughout the European Union through recognised consumer organisations under an accord struck by EU consumer affairs ministers on Thursday.

Under the deal all EU countries will be obliged to recognise their partners' consumer protection organisations, which will be empowered to press cases on behalf of individuals who feel that their rights, laid down in nine EU consumer laws, have been infringed.
European Consumer Affairs Commissioner Emma Bonino told a news conference the accord was a milestone in consumer rights.
Dutch Economic Affairs Minister Anneke van Dok van Weele said the accord had been difficult to reach because it required some countries -- notably Germany and Britain -- to change their ways.
"It has been difficult because it does require change and a measure of harmonisation in the member states," she told the news conference.

At the end of the meeting Germany, which wanted to limit the accord's scope to four EU laws rather than nine, was still opposed to the legislation, but that will not prevent formal adooption by the others.
Britain had held out against the law because it has a unique two-week period in which complaints are cleared before going to a consumer body.
Lack of redress in consumer problems has been seen as a barrier to the real success of the EU's border free market as people have been afraid to buy outside their own country.
